title: The Spiritual Sacrifice and the Fulfillment of Scripture
english: Regarding number. You know that if we do not conceive something as necessary and do not desire to report it to another, how can we ever say 'thus and thus', when we know that we have not sat down to say what we intended? And this one therefore says: 'I have reported and I have spoken'. Since none of your thoughts is like 'I have reported and I have spoken'. It can also be taken this way: 'I have reported' according to the intention, according to the thought, and 'I have spoken' perceptibly according to the utterance; for first it is necessary to conceive, then thus to speak.

Regarding: 'They were increased beyond number'? —the thoughts, to which none is similar. You did not desire sacrifice and offering. Therefore he says: 'He brought me up out of the pit of misery and out of the mire of filth, having set my feet upon a rock, having directed my steps' (Ps 40:2). How much it was necessary to sacrifice and to offer as a burnt offering to God regarding these Christological words and the even greater benefits! But you did not desire the perceptible burnt offerings, the bodily sacrifices from the slaughter of animals and others, the shadowy ones. 'A body he has prepared for me' (Ps 40:6). Instead of these, the apostle has interpreted that this body is the logical and bloodless sacrifice. When therefore a greater sacrifice is found, then he no longer wants the former; they are no longer desired by him.

Let not the [words] of the Diimorites trouble you; for they say: 'Do you see that [it is] a body'? —for the one saying 'a body he has prepared for me', this he says as 'only'; for even one having a perfect man has a body, but not only. And I said the psalm was one-personed from the beginning; for from the beginning to the end the same speaking person has entered. Just as he said here: 'but a body he has prepared for me', and in the following he says: 'those seeking my soul, let them seek it'. Behold, he has a soul also, behold, he has a body also.

And since the word is concerning the perceptible sacrifices superseded by the Spirit, he spoke of the succeeding sacrifice. It is not the soul that becomes the sacrifice according to this meaning, but the body. And it is also good that [it is not] 'he prepared', but himself 'he has prepared', 'the Holy Spirit having come upon' Mary 'and the power of the Most High having overshadowed her' (Lk 1:35). Because of this, you no longer desired those sacrifices and offerings, since 'a body he has prepared for me' which is to be offered on behalf of all. And this can be said: because of this, [he] th...

You did not desire a physical sacrifice and offering, since I have prepared for us a body, which we are able to perform as a sacred rite and sacrifice to you; 'I urge you through mercies to present your bodies as a logical sacrifice' (Rom 12:1). In other [interpretations] it is said: 'And you have prepared ears for me.' One interpreter says this: since you did not desire a sensory sacrifice and offering, 'you have prepared ears for me,' through which I hear those things concerning the things made manifest by the sensory, such as the intellectual sacrifice of understanding: 'sacrifice to God a sacrifice of understanding.' Furthermore, if you call me to a lecture, you no longer seek sensory things being performed, so that what is said might be like: 'The Lord's instruction opens my ears' (Ps 119:16). An unmusical man does not have ears for hearing musical words.

And another of the interpreters said: 'You have dug out ears for me,' since you removed their dullness, you removed that which obstructs hearing. Furthermore: regarding Jesus, how do we receive him? —I said that the 196 allegories are not smoothed out to match the histories. And often I omitted the matter of Abraham and the two women. I said to you that the soul of Jesus is not an unshakeable essence. It is of the same kind as the others, and everything it has that is good, it has from the Word of God. Since therefore it also has the ability to hear well, it has that from the Savior. It surpasses the temple in which it is housed.

7 You did not seek burnt offerings and [things] concerning sin. Nor did you seek, nor did you still delight in the things of the shadow. 'What multitude of your sacrifices to me [is there]? I am full. I do not want the burnt offerings of rams and the fat of lambs' (Ps 50:6). 8 Then he said: 'Behold, I have come' (Isa 6:8). Then I, for whom a body was prepared, said: 'Behold, I have come,' instead of [saying]: since the purpose of his coming is this, to receive the end of the shadow, so that sacrifices and burnt offerings are no longer brought, I have come, in order to fulfill the sacrifice by becoming a burnt offering.

8 It has been written in a heading of a book concerning me. The heading of a book is called 'all inspired Scripture'; for the main point of the Scripture is the life [rule of life] concerning Christ. According to a second account, let it also be said concerning others; for if the coming were not about to happen, the old writings would not have prefigured the Gospel. Furthermore: was this written during the Pentateuch? —He says every Scripture is a book, whose heading is the end for which the writings are given, which is salvation, the coming. title: Opposition of Wills and Spiritual Food
english: Therefore, was the world foretold for this reason? So that He might bring the generation of the world to its completion through humans, and after this generation of humans, so that the epidemic might take place. 'Lamb' is 'of God, who takes away the sin of the world' (John 1:29). Regarding the saying that Adam transgressed 'through disobedience' and the Savior 'through obedience' is justified (Rom 5:19), it is not making a comparison concerning the Savior, who is a type of the one to come, since Adam himself 'is a type of the one to come'; 'this great mystery is, and I say it refers to Christ and the Church' (Eph 5:32).

But since it is not entirely, if a book is said to be, it must be taken according to perception; Ezekiel hears from God: 'open your mouth' (Ezek 3:3), and he sees a book upon the hand of God, and says: 'take it and eat, and your belly shall be filled' (Ezek 3:3). 'And I ate', he says, 'and it became sweetness in my belly'. And he says: 'this book is written within and without' (Ezek 3:3). According to the spiritual and intelligible things it is written within, according to the sensible and manifest things without. But the wise man devours both and finds harmony between the symbols and the originals.

And in Isaiah he says again: 'and these words shall be as the words of the book of the sealed, if they give it to a man knowing letters, saying: take, read. He says: I cannot, for it is sealed' (Isa 29:11). And the illiterate man says: 'I do not know letters'. He was asking whether it differed if it were sealed or not sealed. And we take again the God-breathed Scripture, the one knowing letters but unable to read because of the placed seals being the circumcised people, and the one not knowing letters being from the Gentiles.

'To do, O God, your will I have desired' (Ps 40:8). Therefore 'I said: behold, I have come' (Heb 10:7), since the will was desired to do your will after you did not desire me for sacrifice and offering. Those who hold false doctrines concerning Christ say that there are different wills; for even here he says: 'I have come, I desire to do your will', in the Gospel: 'I have descended from heaven not to do human will, but the will of him who sent me' (John 6:38). Therefore, concerning those saying that there are two wills, we say that: the different wills occur either according to more or less or...

In opposition. The one progressing in virtue desires righteousness, and the one perfected [does too], and the will of the perfected is not the same as that of the one progressing or the one being led in. For there becomes either a multitude or a duality of wills according to the more and the less, and it also happens in opposition, when one chooses good things and another evil, and one wills to be saved and another to sin. Therefore, such a will as this, to approach the Son having opposition, is the extreme of impiety.

Furthermore, I also direct [this] toward the Manichaeans. One must act toward these: the will of the Savior is found to be good; for he says, having come down from heaven, 'that I might do the will of God' (John 6:38). And to do the will of God is good. And again: 'The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost' (Luke 19:10). And again: 'If you wish, you are able to cleanse me' (Mark 10:51). If this is the will of the Son, he wills all things that are beneficial. But since the will of the Father is being opposite to him, I leave it to you to consider. If it is found according to the more and the less in wills and in disposition, then both the Father and the Son will have a disposition, that is, a way of acting, and the Father is no longer without body, nor is the essence without connection. Nor is it to be said according to the more and the less, nor in opposition; for the will of the Son is demonstrated to be good. Yet it is not right according to God to say, however, that this is his will, to perfect the will of the Father. It is not right according to God to say [this]. Nor is it opposite, nor according to the more and the less. Therefore, one must take these things regarding the man.

And 'your law in the midst of my belly' (Psalm 119:11). It is spiritual food containing [itself] in the belly of the inner man. And the law, which is evident everywhere, is spiritual food; for it is not sensible food. This belly is often praised, and in the [psalm]: 'From the fear of you in the belly we have received' (Psalm 119:11). And just as this belly receives in the belly from the divine spirit—which is the fear of God—so also it receives divine food into itself. No longer desiring your sacrifice or offering or burnt offerings, having the spiritual law as food. I have evangelized righteousness in a great church. 'Great church' is the one of the...

title: The Union of Truth and Mercy
english: Consisting of great things, concerning which Paul says, 'we speak wisdom among the perfect' (1 Cor 2:6), so that the sum of these is a 'great church.' This is not the righteousness according to the law, about which the apostle says, 'having become blameless according to the righteousness in the law' (Rom 3:19). This then righteousness I preached to the great church; for if the letter and the shadow were not preached to the great [ones], but to infants.

But what kind of righteousness? —about which the Savior was saying, 'unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees' (Matt 5:20), is this not according to the shadow? Therefore yours—of the disciples—the Savior says, let the righteousness exceed theirs. And he says that theirs was with ignorance. Because of this, let us not be ignorant of the righteousness of God, but let us preach it.

10 Behold, my lips I will not restrain. 'Lips' here means the word. Often when he is called to say something to small and imperfect men, we restrain our lips; we do not have them released, but we descend with them, we speak cryptically, we speak proverbially, and our lips are restrained. But when to the perfect and a great church, since he does not restrain his lips, since he does not hinder them from speaking anything. And it is possible also to say this: as the [psalmist says]: 'and in his law he will meditate day and night' (Ps 1:2). He never restrains his lips, always bringing forth the words of God. And the 'always' hear it thus: as it is necessary and as it is fitting to do this; for even if he is silent, he speaks in his mind, and even while sleeping, when he sleeps as a righteous man, he does this with the word. And through silence, he remembers something good.

10–11 Lord, you have known my righteousness (Ps 26:3). Since much of what is said has testified to himself—for 'to preach righteousness in a great church' is great and, so that I may say this, beyond man—he says to God: 'you have known my righteousness' (Ps 26:3). This [righteousness], which I announce, I possess and have practiced according to it. And if the psalm were even speaking about the man of the Savior, that: since he did not know sin, but the sin that has come to be, it is productive of righteousness. And this is also possible: even if some, being ignorant, speak blasphemy against me, but you know my righteousness. As also Susanna said: 'you know that...'

What false things testify against me? I have not hidden your truth in my heart. He who has known the righteousness of God does not hide the truth joined to it in his heart. Truth is called joined to righteousness when it says: 'Truth has risen from the earth, and righteousness has stooped from heaven' (Ps 85:11). Regarding the Savior, he says righteousness is stooping from heaven; for he says: 'He bent the heaven and came down.' And 'risen from the earth' means having reached the end of the visitation. But it can also be understood thus: when from the earth, that good and beautiful soul has risen after having heard the word and having been fruitful. Therefore righteousness stoops from heaven. And in another psalm he says: 'Mercy and truth met, righteousness and peace kissed' (Ps 85:10). Those who read histories find that wars and disturbances arise from unrighteousness. But truth has the mercy of God; for if God does not show mercy, no one is able to know the truth, how much and what it is. Therefore 'mercy and truth met.' And mercy is also possible, such as he who loves his neighbor as himself is merciful to his neighbor and himself requires the same mercy from him; for indeed the truth is made manifest. Just as righteousness leads peace, so also the mercy of truth. Moreover, both are one and the same. If then Jesus and his words are ashamed, his truth is ashamed. 'And I have spoken my salvation' (Ps 116:16). The confession of the truth is my salvation. If he also says the truth concerning Christ, he again says Christ is the salvation, and 'I have spoken my salvation and revealed your truth.' I speak of the salvation being the Christ whom I make manifest. 'I have not hidden your mercy and your truth from a great assembly' (Ps 51:1). We say that mercy is joined to the truth. And 'a great assembly' means those from the Gentiles who have believed, having been gathered from all the Gentiles. And the wise man says this, and Jesus also according to the man. 'And you, Lord, do not distance your mercies from me' (Ps 51:1). I have come to your mercies, blamelessly and as is necessary. Do not therefore distance them, so that I may remain such. 'Let the [mercy] quickly overtake us...'
The text ends abruptly with a fragment of a quote.
